purpose: Separate Trusted Trend Candidates (evidence-backed) from Question Demand Signals (audience-question detection only). No social or consumer-media claim may become content without an independent official, scientific or primary source.

trusted_trend_radar.description: Only pre-approved official, scientific, professional and high-quality editorial sources may create a Trend Candidate.
trusted_trend_radar.official_social_rule: Official social accounts may point to a topic, but the corresponding official website, original study, guideline or regulator notice remains required as primary_url.

question_demand_radar.description: Reddit, forums, Turkish search trends, social comments, DMs and popular health media may be used only as Question Demand Signals.
question_demand_radar.answers_only: What are medical students or professionals repeatedly asking about?

steps: Check whether reliable primary, guideline or scientific evidence exists.
Create an Evidence File only if the answer can be supported.
If evidence is weak, conflicting or unavailable, state that clearly or discard. Never fill the gap with social-media claims.

output_levels.VERIFIED_ANSWER_CARD: Simple official, time-sensitive or procedural answer.
output_levels.EVIDENCE_BRIEF: Recurring question with a concise, source-backed explanation.
output_levels.EVIDENCE_FILE: Complex clinical, scientific, public-health, education or career question requiring structured evidence, limitations and practical implications.
output_levels.QUESTION_BRIEF: Normalized demand question awaiting or lacking primary evidence — not publishable content.

hard_rules: No question, trend or audience demand signal may become content without an independent scientific, official or primary source.
AI may normalize questions, classify demand and summarize verified evidence.
AI must never infer an answer from demand signals or invent missing evidence.
